body: I think it was a very good comment, there were really funny and beautiful scenes, Haluk Bilginer and Feyzaz Yigit played the characters very well, it was very good. As someone who watched the original version, I was a little shy, wondering if it was a ridiculous job, but I think it was a very good comment, I recommend it.

I'm usually very skeptical about remakes, but this adaptation of 'The Intouchables' is a masterpiece. I re-watched the original right after seeing this, and honestly, the Turkish version feels much more sincere. Feyyaz Yigit and Haluk Bilginer are the perfect match; their energy and dynamic are flawless. The way they localized the story to fit Turkish culture without losing the soul of the original is incredible. It's rare to see a remake that brings its own unique flavor so successfully.

Even though I watched it knowing it was an adaptation and constantly compared it to the original in my mind, I quite liked the way the screenwriters and directors localized the story / made it specific to our culture.

The drama-comedy balance was also quite good. They did not make the mistake of overly dramatizing Ferruh's story or turning Ferruh into a 'Recep Ivedik' (referencing a crude, slapstick comedy character), which was another plus for the film.

It was a beautiful film that can be watched with pleasure.

7 / 10.

This is hands down the best Turkish movie I have seen in a long time. Even though it is an adaptation of The Intouchables, it does an excellent job of adapting the story to our local culture. It successfully captures the unique traits that define us, making the film feel authentic and relatable rather than just a remake.

The highlight is undoubtedly the acting. I sincerely appreciate and applaud the performances of Haluk Bilginer and Feyyaz Yigit. Their chemistry is natural, captivating, and carries the film effortlessly.

If you are looking for quality storytelling that blends a familiar plot with genuine local spirit, this is a must-watch.

Everyone should go see this movie. I didn't have the chance to watch it in IMAX, but in terms of production, performances, and script, it was truly top-tier. I'm definitely adding it to the list of films I'd watch again. Those who have the chance should watch it in IMAX. Seeing Feyyaz Yigit in a film like this genuinely made me happy. And I don't think it's surprising that a talented actor like Haluk Bilginer portrayed this character so well - he was outstanding too.
